study.title: Neuronal Specificity of Acupuncture in Alzheimer's Disease and Mild Cognitive Impairment Patients: A Functional MRI Study
study.study_design: Randomized controlled experiment with single-block fMRI design; AD and MCI patients randomly divided into real acupuncture point group and sham acupuncture point group; HC experienced only real acupuncture point stimulation
study.randomization: AD and MCI patients were randomly divided into two experimental groups
study.population: 21 AD patients (51-77 years old; mean age, 66.9 years old), 14 MCI patients (44-80 years old; mean age, 66.4 years old), and 14 healthy people (57-75 years old; mean age, 66.1 years old)
study.disease_condition: Alzheimer's disease (AD) and mild cognitive impairment (MCI)
study.inclusion_criteria: AD: DSM-IV criteria for dementia and NINCDS-ADRDA criteria for possible or probable AD. MCI: (a) memory impairment on a normalized objective verbal memory test; (b) history of recent worsening memory symptoms; (c) MMSE score of 24 or higher and normal or near-normal performance on other daily living scales; (d) CDR scale of at least 0.5; (e) not meeting the criteria for dementia. HC: (a) no neurological or psychiatric disorders such as stroke, depression, or epilepsy; (b) no neurological deficiencies such as visual or hearing loss; (c) no abnormal findings such as infarction or focal lesion in conventional brain MR imaging; (d) no cognitive complaints. All participants were right-handed.
study.exclusion_criteria: (a) contraindications for MRI such as pacemaker, cardiac defibrillator, implanted material with electric or magnetic system, vascular clips, or mechanical heart valve, cochlear implant, or claustrophobia; (b) history of stroke, psychiatric diseases, drug abuse, severe hypertension, systematic diseases, or intellectual disability

conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: The description states only that sham acupuncture points are used during fMRI acquisition. No information is provided about needle depth, penetration, or device type. 'Sham acupuncture points' (non-acupoints) could involve full-depth insertion (Level 1), superficial insertion (Level 2), or a non-penetrating device (Level 3). Without any depth or penetration detail, tissue level cannot be determined. | RESOLVED: needling at non-acupoints with depth not stated → assumed Level 1 (standard clinical depth)

extraction_notes.note: Table 2 for 'AD with sham acupuncture point stimulation' appears to duplicate the Cerebellum_4_5 right row (coordinates 9, -57, -18; T=4.50; cluster=50) as both first and last entries in the sham section. This duplication was present in the original table and has been faithfully extracted.
No sensory or deqi measures were reported. It is not stated whether deqi, pain, or other needle sensation was assessed or even intended. This is a notable gap for acupuncture specificity research.

No expectancy, credibility, blinding success, or allocation guessing instruments were reported or mentioned. Participants were not assessed for whether they could distinguish real from sham acupuncture.

The paper does not report direct between-group (real vs. sham) statistical comparisons with coordinates or test statistics. The comparison between real and sham groups is described narratively in the discussion rather than with formal statistical contrasts. No formal between-group neuroimaging contrast table is provided.
The paper does not report direct between-group (patients vs. HC) statistical comparisons with coordinates or test statistics. Differences are described by comparing within-group results narratively.

In Table 3 (MCI with real acupuncture), the T-value for Frontal_Inf_Oper is printed as '4,50' with a comma rather than a decimal point, which appears to be an OCR or typesetting artifact for 4.50. This value was extracted as 4.50.

The BA (Brodmann area) column in Tables 2, 3, and 4 uses '/' for most rows where no BA is specified, and only fills in a number for a subset of rows. It is unclear if '/' means not assigned or not applicable. Rows with '/' in the BA column were extracted as brodmann_area_exact: 'not_reported'.

The paper labels the sham points as '10 mm anterior to the corresponding real ones' in Figure 1 caption, while the main text states 'approximately 10 mm next to bilateral Taichong (LR3) or Hegu (LI4).' These descriptions are slightly inconsistent; both have been preserved in extraction.

The post-acupuncture 10-minute scan data were explicitly excluded from analysis ('fMRI data acquired during the three-minute resting-state baseline and three-minute acupuncture administration period were included'). No post-treatment fMRI results are available from this study design.

The paper does not report whether sham acupuncture also involved needle rotation (±180°, 60 times per minute) or if this manipulation was only for real acupuncture. The methods section implies the same procedure was used for both real and sham points: 'All these manipulations were performed by the same two skilled acupuncturists in synchrony.' This has been extracted accordingly but remains ambiguous.
No flip angle information was reported for the fMRI sequence. The sequence section states FA = 90°. This has been captured in the neuroimaging_methods section as part of the sequence description.

The paper describes the MCI RA sham group AVLT immediate score as 22.50±3.02, which appears unusually high relative to the MCI clinical profile described (memory impairment). This may reflect that the MCI SA group happened to have higher baseline scores by chance given the small n=6; no correction was made to the extracted values.

No between-group baseline comparison (RA vs. SA within AD or within MCI) was formally reported, though group sample sizes were small. This limits interpretation of between-group imaging contrasts that were not performed.

The study adopted a single-block design comparing baseline (rest) to acupuncture stimulation within the same session. This is not a classic task-fMRI block design in the traditional sense but uses a boxcar waveform convolved with HRF, consistent with a block/epoch design.
